28e9b855.text:
The Mauradine Centaur of Desolace.

When you use shamanism to empower your people, it demands harmony with nature. The wind answers your call because it chooses to. You are its champion, and it becomes the power that lets your people soar. However, the Mauradine have no respect for this balance.

This particular clan has only wielded this power for selfish gain. Hunting parties flying across the plains to stalk their foes, spellcasters channeling great storms to burn villages. And even this is not enough. They have created totems of hideous power, forcing the elements to bend to their will.

It is not for us to decide Azeroth's desires, but one thing is clear. The Mauradine are no friends to the elements.
28e9b855.title: The Walks of Shaman

57d4e03b.text:
The Mirefin Murlocs of Dustwallow Marsh.

Murlocs have an innate connection to water as any seafolk, but in a curious way. Many species can recognize the elements in nature without tapping directly into it. The murlocs, however, not only can call upon water, but wield it with surprising intelligence.

Their oracles have a curious affinity for restorative magic. Water is a source of healing for all creatures, from hydration to medicine, but the murlocs managed to tap into its even deeper sources of power. What takes some adepts decades to master, some murlocs seem to be born with this gift.

If this were any other $c, one would think this to be a blessing. But they are murlocs, after all. Their healing magic is as much a weapon as any other, keeping their hunters sharp and their shores battle-ready. Using totems is curious for a species like this, but make no mistake. They are as corrupt as their masters.
57d4e03b.title: The Walks of Shaman

bc13bd7f.text:
The Lost Ones of the Swamp of Sorrows.

Earth is the element of fortitude and steadiness. A $c capable of harnessing the earth's power can guarantee their people sturdy homes and durable warriors. What could otherwise flatten another combatant can be shrugged off by one gifted by the powers of earth.

It can also be used to crumble others.

When left to their devices, the Lost Ones rarely interfere with the goings on of other cultures. They stalk about in a mindless fugue state as if they don't truly belong anywhere. The only thing that offers them grounding is the elements.

Unlike the others mentioned, it is not necessarily believed that the Lost Ones have a genuine desire for harm. Earth offers them solace in their aimless wandering. However, with this comes their dependence.

Calling on the elements for aid is one thing, but demanding their presence is another. They are our guides, not our crutches. Now their totems are just as twisted as the Lost Ones themselves.
bc13bd7f.title: The Walks of Shaman

214529|859a347e.name: Brave Stonetorch
214529|859a347e.text:
Now that I've seen this land and have heard the sound of the earth here, I think I am glad I made the journey. 

Ah, forgive me. I am thinking aloud. I am called Stonetorch, and I come here seeking knowledge of a brilliant white stone that some say fell from the sky and came to rest in the hills over yonder. Some among my people believe that this is a tear wept from An'she, the eye of the Earth Mother herself.

I don't know if I believe that, but I do intend to see this phenomenon for myself and make my own judgement.

536-accept.name: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle
536-accept.text:
Transferred from the Stormwind city guard to Southshore, a town that should be abandoned by the looks of it... Smell of the harbor day and night.

Not to mention ol' Redpath... Wants me to take care of the murlocs. Ha! 

I can barely rouse myself to go out to some of the pockets of the overgrown fish down the Western Strand. If you would go in my place and take care of them, I'd appreciate it.
536-accept.title: Down the Coast

538-complete.name: Loremaster Dibbs
538-complete.text:
Ah yes, I remember Milton.  A bookworm, no doubt.  Bless him.

And he's right.  The Ruins of Alterac still hold stores of knowledge in danger of being lost!

Ogres now dwell in Alterac, and they don't care much for higher learning.
538-complete.title: Southshore

540-accept.name: Loremaster Dibbs
540-accept.text:
Those beastly ogres now reside within Alterac's ruins, and I shudder to think what they're doing with the precious books still there.  You must recover what you can!

Enter the Ruins of Alterac and search for tomes looted by the ogres.  Get whatever you can find and bring them to me, but also seek out one book in particular: The Arm of Gri'lek.  It contains ancient troll lore that I must learn, and the Ruins of Alterac was the last known location of an intact copy of this book.
540-accept.title: Preserving Knowledge

96016-accept.name: Veyric Thunderhame
96016-accept.text:
Ye did good, and I can see yer itchin' fer yer reward. Sorry tae say, I'm not exactly a $r of many possessions.

<Veyric gestures broadly at his remote location.>

Tell ye what, though. I hear a troll named the Windwatcher lives out in the Alterac Mountains. He's a powerful $c himself, and an expert in storm elementals. If ye bring that there elemental core to him, I bet he can make ye a weapon worthy of yer victory.
96016-accept.title: The Tempest's Weapons

96135-complete.name: Veyric Thunderhame
96135-complete.text:
Can ye feel it, $N? The breeze sings of yer victory. If ye hadn't earned the elements' respect before, ye sure have now.

Walk tall, $c. Yer a credit to our order.
96135-complete.title: Heed My Call

96135-progress.name: Veyric Thunderhame
96135-progress.text: I can feel the storm in my belly, $N. Have ye dispersed it yet?
96135-progress.title: Heed My Call
